BASIC BRAKE SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS
TSB Revision
BASIC BRAKE SYSTEM
35A-14
INSPECTION PROCEDURE6: Squealing, Groaning or Chattering Noise when Brakes are Applied
DIAGNOSIS
STEP 1. Check the brake drums and lining or 
brake disc and pads for wear or cutting.
Q: Is there wear or cutting?
YES : Repair or replace the part. Then go to Step 
7.
NO : Go to Step 2.
STEP 2. Check the calipers for rust.
Q: Is there rust?
YES : Remove the rust. Then go to Step 7.
NO : Go to Step 3.
STEP 3. Check the lining parts for damage.
If equipped with rear disc brakes, go to Step 6.
Q: Is there damage?
YES : Repair or replace the part. Then go to Step 
7.
NO : Go to Step 4.
STEP 4. Check whether the lining is dirty or 
greasy.
Q: Is the lining dirty or greasy?
YES : Clean or replace the part. Then go to Step 
7.
NO : Go to Step 5.
STEP 5. Check whether the shoe hold-down 
springs are weak or the shoe-hold-down pins 
and springs are loose or damaged.
Q: Is there fault?
YES : Repair or replace the part. Then go to Step 
7.
NO : Go to Step 6.
STEP 6. Adjust the brake pedal or brake booster 
pushrod.
Refer to P.35A-18 or P.35A-32.
Q: Is the adjustment value come?
YES : Adjust. Then go to Step 7.
NO : Go to Step 7.
STEP 7. Recheck symptom.
Q: Is the symptom eliminated?
YES : Diagnosis is complete.
NO : Start over at step 1. If a new symptom 
surfaces, refer to the symptom chart.
INSPECTION PROCEDURE 7: Squealing Noise when Brakes are not Applied
DIAGNOSIS
STEP 1. Check whether the backing plate is bent or loose 
and interfering with the drum. <Vehicles equipped with 
rear drum brakes>
If equipped with rear disc brakes, go to Step 4.
Q: Is there fault?
YES : Replace the part. Then go to Step 10.
NO : Go to Step 2.
STEP 2. Check whether the drum is damaged due to 
interference with the backing plate or shoe.
Q: Is there damage?
YES : Replace the part. Then go to Step 10.
NO : Go to Step 3.
